message:
Fix KeyExpiration when a zero time value has a timezone

When a zero time value is loaded from JSON or a DB in a way that
assigns it the local timezone, it does not roudtrip in JSON as a
value for which IsZero returns true. This causes KeyExpiry to be
treated as a far past value instead of a nilish value.

See https://github.com/golang/go/issues/57040

body:
Thank you, much appreciated, for this change I would need a integration test that first verify the problem, so something that when ran in sqlite/postgres mode returns pass/fail respectively, and then when this change is applied change to pass/pass.

If you have time to look at it would be great, or else I can see what I have time to do next week.

I recon that a fix for this issue also would merit a changelog entry.

The unit test I added would fail prior to this change, and now passes. It really actually has nothing to do with the database, but rather the `KeyExpiry` time object having a non-UTC timezone. Just the postgresql driver being used (pgx) happens to put all times into the local timezone, and the sqllite driver in use does not - but I guess that could change on the part of either driver since the the time represents the same instant of the zero value, so I think the test I added is the appropriate verification of this. If you disagree I can look at adding an integration test. I'll update the PR to add a changelog entry.
Integration tests to ensure full roundtrip via both drivers would be necessary. Both for this change and to ensure regressions, we have had libraries introduce silent failures before.

I guess it really depends on the timezone the tests run in - the existing integration tests should trip it as long as the timezone the headscale server runs in is non-UTC. I suspect on the integration tests the timezone is set to UTC and hence doesn't happen. I can take a look next week and see how hard it would be to introduce that, I'm not familiar with your integration test setup.

message: Ensure that postgresql is used for all tests when env var is set
Pass through value of HEADSCALE_INTEGRATION_POSTGRES env var

Add test for registration with auth key in alternate timezone

## PR Summary

The pull request titled "Fix 764" addresses an issue related to the handling of zero time values in the Headscale application when using a PostgreSQL backend. The problem arises when a zero time value is loaded from JSON or a database, resulting in it being assigned the local timezone. This causes the value to not round-trip correctly in JSON, leading to the `KeyExpiry` being interpreted as a far past value instead of a nilish value. The author references a related issue in the Go programming language's GitHub repository. The PR includes a unit test that verifies the fix, ensuring that the `KeyExpiry` behaves as expected after the change. The author notes that the issue is not directly related to the database type but rather to how the PostgreSQL driver handles timezones compared to the SQLite driver. The PR aims to resolve the issue identified in issue #764, which describes a failure in activating Tailscale clients when using a PostgreSQL backend.

## Objectives from Linked Issues

The linked issue #764 describes a bug where Tailscale clients authenticate successfully with Headscale when configured to use a PostgreSQL backend but subsequently get stuck in a loop, continuously refreshing keys. The issue is characterized by the following sequence of events: after the initial payload exchange, the client sends a payload with `read_only=true`, and Headscale responds with a `KeyExpiry` set to an incorrect zero time value. This incorrect value leads to the client repeatedly sending the same payload, preventing it from progressing to a state where it sends a payload with `read_only=false`. The objective of the linked issue is to identify and resolve the underlying cause of this behavior, ensuring that Tailscale clients can successfully activate when using a PostgreSQL backend, similar to their behavior with SQLite.

## Comments Summary

In the comments on the pull request, the reviewer, kradalby, expresses appreciation for the changes made by the author, mpoindexter. However, kradalby requests the addition of an integration test that would verify the problem by running tests in both SQLite and PostgreSQL modes.
